newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives split on Europe - opposition.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives split on Europe - opposition.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party stepped up its attack on the ruling Conservatives over Europe on Sunday, saying Prime Minister John Major's party was bitterly divided over the issue of a single currency.

Labour foreign affairs spokesman Robin Cook said a survey of the election literature of 100 Conservative candidates in the May 1 election showed "a clear majority" were flouting the party's official policy on monetary union by promising they would never back a single currency.
Major favours a wait-and-see approach but Cook said plenty of Conservatives backed an openly Euro-sceptic line.
"The Tory (Conservative) truce on the single currency has collapsed," Cook said in a statement. "Tory election literature reveals the Tory party as divided, dogmatic and disloyal over Europe."

The Conservatives and Labour both have similar policies on a proposed single currency. Both say they will decide whether to join a European single currency when monetary union is closer to becoming a reality, and will hold a referendum to ask voters whether they approve of joining.

But dissent about a single currency has dogged Major's party, with many members wary of closer ties with Brussels. A millionaire businessman has offered campaign funds to Conservative candidates who oppose a single currency, and says he expects the offer to be taken up by around 200 -- almost a third of all Conservative candidates.
"The Tory skirmishes over Europe in the past parliament look set to become full-blown civil war in the next parliament," Cook said.
Conservative Defence Secretary Michael Portillo, a prominent Euro-sceptic, said it was "perfectly reasonable" for candidates to stray from the official party line on Europe.

"The Labour Party has sought to produce a situation where all MPs are merely automata, who are programmed...and sent off to say exactly the same thing in the same moment at the same place," he said. "That isn't real democracy."
